html:
The Vilela are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in northern Argentina, once living along the Bermejo river and in what are now Salta, Santiago del Estero and Chaco provinces.

They were hunters, fishers and gatherers of the dry forest. Their language is grouped with that of the Lule in a small Lule-Vilela family. Spanish Jesuit missions gathered some of them in the 1700s, and raids and wars with neighbours such as the Qom and Abipones reduced them further. Only a handful of people still remembered the Vilela language in recent decades, and today some families in Chaco province claim Vilela descent.
sum: The Vilela are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in northern Argentina, once living along the Bermejo river and in what are now Salta, Santiago del Estero and Chaco provinces.
